finding: The install enables the built-in Local provider but never assigns it to a user group, so the installed model is invisible in the picker and chat answers 403 ACCESS_DENIED — the user must still visit Settings, which INV-2 forbids.
resolution: Verified against get_for_user (INNER JOIN user_group_llm_providers) and user_has_access_to_provider — both required, no admin bypass. ensureLocalProvider now assigns the default/Users group when the provider has no group, leaves an existing arrangement alone, and reports a human-actionable problem when it cannot.

finding: The seeded row ships enabled but the boot health scan probes it (has_credential_for("none") is true, so the unconfigured-row skip does not cover it) and auto-disables it on any transport failure — an offline first boot permanently defeats INV-5.
resolution: Verified in connection_health.rs: the skip is !has_credential(), and Unhealthy calls disable_repository. The boot scan now also skips built-in anonymous rows, with the reasoning in-code. TEST-21 added and verified RED without the fix (it caught it on a NETWORKED box by asserting the row is never PROBED, not merely still enabled).

finding: TEST-1 asserts row.enabled immediately after boot while a fire-and-forget scan can flip that column — it races the mechanism it polices.
resolution: TEST-21 added: waits past the scan and asserts last_health_check_status stays 'untested', which is deterministic regardless of network state.

finding: The loopback git fixture TEST-4/5/7 depend on is unreachable (clone_repository validates PUBLIC_HTTP_OR_HTTPS unconditionally); and its 401-on-Authorization gate is inoperative anyway, since libgit2 supplies credentials only in response to a challenge.
resolution: Independently found and fixed before this audit landed: the fixture was deleted and INV-1 re-proven at the credential decision point. The auditor's second half — that the fixture's gate could not have worked even if reachable — is a stronger argument for the same conclusion and is recorded in DEC-14.

finding: TEST-6 asserts the model row exists and is enabled but never that it is REACHABLE by a user, so it passes unchanged while the group-assignment gap makes the model unusable.
resolution: TEST-6 now asserts the model is visible via GET /api/user-llm-providers for a non-admin member of the default group — the endpoint the model picker actually reads.

finding: The LFS client carries a 30-minute ABSOLUTE request timeout, capping a 5.68 GB blob at a sustained ~3.2 MB/s floor; below that the default install always fails.
resolution: Verified: Client::builder().timeout(60*30) applies to the whole request incl. the body stream. NOT fixed here — raising it weakens a security bound in shared code that closed a Medium finding, and choosing the minimum supported connection speed for a first-run default is a product call, not mine. Recorded as a known limitation in the design doc + DEC-15 and escalated to the owner in HUMAN_FEEDBACK.

finding: deriveViewState checks the terminal download record BEFORE installing/stage, so a retry renders 'failed' with a live button for the whole provider leg, allowing concurrent orchestrations.
resolution: Corroborated by the correctness angle independently. Ordering inverted so a running orchestration outranks any past outcome; a regression test covers both the provider and runtime legs.

finding: isDefaultModelInstalled ignores `enabled` on both provider and model, so a disabled either still renders 'you can start chatting' — contradicting its own doc.
resolution: Both enabled flags now required, with a unit test and a mounted component test for each half.

finding: The design names seven step states as needing GALLERY coverage; the change registers skip:true entries and proves them in a jsdom mount instead, so none is seen by gate:ui's runtime-health / contrast / visual pass.
resolution: Deliberate, recorded as DEC-16. The onboarding module is crawlOnly and its sibling steps map the same way; a bespoke cassette for one step would diverge from every other Onboarding surface. The states ARE proven, by mounting the real component. Flagged to the owner as the one place the shipped approach differs from the design's wording.

finding: A user lacking llm_local_runtime::versions_read is silently blinded — loadVersions early-returns without error so hasInstalledRuntime reports false, then listAvailable 403s; the Install control is gated only on llm_models::create though the flow needs several more permissions.
resolution: The control now gates on the whole set the flow needs (models::create, providers::edit, providers::assign_groups, runtime versions_read/create/update); a user missing any of them gets the informational panel instead of a button that 403s partway through.

finding: TEST-5 wrapped every assertion in `if !raced_to_completion`, so it passed vacuously whenever the cancel lost the race — the comment claimed a skip that did not exist.
resolution: Already gone: TEST-5 was rewritten before this audit landed to drive a real FAILURE (unconditionally reachable) rather than race a cancel. No conditional remains.

finding: The 'cancelled' view state is unreachable from any real store path — the cancel action removes the row and both load paths filter cancelled out — so its explanatory note never renders.
resolution: Verified against cancelLlmModelDownload, subscribeToDownloadProgress and _loadExistingDownloads. The dead state and its note are removed rather than kept as decoration; cancelling restores the offer, and the test now asserts that.

finding: When the snapshot is absent, waitForRuntimeDownload re-lists versions every 500ms for the full 15-minute deadline — ~1800 requests.
resolution: The server-side re-list is now floored at one per 5s while the local poll stays at 500ms.

finding: findInstalledVersionId matches on engine alone and its result is passed to setDefaultVersion, so the step can promote an unrelated llama.cpp version to system default.
resolution: Now matches the full {engine, version, platform, arch, backend} tuple the step actually requested.

finding: install() has no re-entrancy guard, so two overlapping orchestrations can run concurrently; only the weights leg is de-duplicated, and only server-side.
resolution: Corroborated by the conformance angle's same-root finding. install() now early-returns when already installing; the viewState ordering fix removes the window that made it reachable.

finding: The step store is never reset when the wizard is left — unlike its two siblings — so a stale error re-renders the failure alert on a later, unrelated visit.
resolution: A reset action was added and wired at both sites where OnboardingPage already resets the sibling step stores. It clears only this store — the download stores are deliberately untouched so a transfer survives leaving the wizard (INV-6).

finding: TEST-7's doc claims every client handle is dropped, but drop(instance) drops a serde_json::Value; the body was already consumed and each request builds its own client.
resolution: The doc-comment now states what the test actually proves — that the work reaches its own conclusion with no client interaction — rather than overclaiming a dropped connection.

finding: Nothing verifies the upstream repo path/filename the whole feature hinges on actually exists, so a wrong name would ship green and every real install would 404. (Auditor flagged as unconfirmed from its environment.)
resolution: Verified out of band against the real upstream: `git ls-remote https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF` exits 0 with no credential, and the HF model API lists `Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf` among its 28 files. Both values are CORRECT. The coverage gap is real and cannot be closed by a test (the design forbids hitting real HF), so the verification and its date are recorded in the descriptor and DEC-15.
